title: Frankenstein (trimmed letters)
purpose: Real public-domain control. Walton's Arctic letters are coherent; the checker should stay quiet except for mysteries the text itself opens.
notes: Taken from Gutenberg Frankenstein, Letters 1–2, trimmed to ~900 words each.
No planted faults. False positives here mean the tool cannot be trusted on literary prose.
Expect open threads about Walton's voyage and the stranger he will meet — those are the novel's job.

tolerate.why: Epistolary openings are allowed to withhold who the stranger is and how the voyage ends.

must_not_fire.why: Continuing north, hiring a ship, and writing home are consistent with Letter 1. Do not treat travel progress as a contradiction of earlier plans.
